worldPlatePrompt: One continuous single-frame view at night and low tide, from a little above the gravel wharf at the foot of a flight of stone canal locks on a cold fog-desert diamond coast in the nineteen-twenties, like the Namib near Luderitz: a small walled harbour basin of black still water with one low gravel barge and two punts at the wharf, a long low rubble breakwater with a small stone sea lock at its far end under a sheer dark headland, and beyond the breakwater a wide flat floor of wet black wave-cut rock bared by the tide, a few warm lanterns on tall tripods over gravel pits on it, a deep channel along the headland's foot, and a long low bank of sea fog lying pale on the open sea. A bright full moon high over the sea, cold silver light, warm orange lantern light. Painterly realism. No people, no text, nothing modern.
coverPrompt: Minimalist stylised thumbnail poster: a low gravel barge moored at a stone wharf at night, and out on a dark tidal rock floor a single tall tripod with one glowing lantern over a gravel pit, under a bright full moon. One bold, simple, high-contrast silhouette that reads at thumbnail size; flat limited palette of deep blue-black night, silver moonlight and one warm amber lantern glow. Strong negative space, soft film grain. Square. No people, no text.
story: Tonight's low tide has bared the rock floor beyond the breakwater, and the gravel barge goes up the locks to the washing plant at dawn, with the whole class as her night crew. Take a punt out to a gravel pit, fit a regression model to the test sacks in R, and choose your answer to fill the sacks you carry: one at the pit under the sea lock, two at the pit on the rock platform, three at the far pit on its outer edge. Carry each load back to the barge and stack it aboard; the sacks are invented, but every model is the real one.

before.label: The small punt to the sea lock pit
before.desc: a short way along the wharf's stone edge on the side toward the sea lock, afloat against it below the wharf, a small flat-bottomed wooden punt, a punting pole laid along her, her line made fast to a short timber post on the wharf

after.label: The small punt to the sea lock pit
after.desc: standing far in from the left edge of the frame, with at least 1200 px of the 3072 px width of plain dark stone retaining wall and level bare gravel, with no object, no pebbles and no cast shadow, between it and that edge, nearest first: close by on the wharf, a broad waist-high heap of the diamond gravel waiting for the barges, rounded water-worn beach pebbles of many colours, slate grey, ochre, rust-red and milky quartz, wet and glinting in the moonlight, the whole heap and its foot starting no closer than 1200 px from the left edge; beside it, toward the centre, a small black iron steam crane on a timber base, its jib swung out over the heap and its hook and chains hanging inboard of the heap's crest, cold and at rest, its timber base, boiler, chimney and flywheel starting no closer than 1300 px from the left edge; and beyond them the gravel of the wharf running level to the foot of a straight stone stair with low side walls that climbs the bank beside the lowest lock's tall dark wall to the terrace a full storey above, a heavy iron chain slung slack across the whole width of the stair's foot with a padlock hanging from it; above the terrace only darkness

On the far left, the left half of the calm view directly behind the viewer: the wide wet rock floor stretching away inland, broken by low ribs of black rock and still pools, joining its other half cleanly at the seam directly behind you; to the left, the flat wet rock of the platform running back level across low ribs and pools to a lantern on a tall tripod over a pit near the deep channel, far off, and beyond it the dark headland and the sea lock's single lit window; left of centre, a few strides from the viewer, cut deep into the flat rock near its edge, the gravel pit: a deep square shaft in the black rock with wet, rounded, many-coloured beach gravel and seawater at its bottom, a heavy wooden windlass frame straddling its mouth with a rope running down from the drum to a bucket, a wooden rocker cradle on the rock beside it, a few heavy canvas sacks of wet gravel, each tied at the neck lying loose by the rim, and beside the windlass a tall marker pole with a lantern in an iron cage at its top; dead ahead in the centre, a short way ahead, the platform's outer lip, where the flat rock ends in a low step down into the sea, dark kelp lying heaped on the step, low swells breaking white over the lip; right of centre, beyond the lip the dark sea under the full moon high in the sky, a silver path on the water, and a little way out a long low wall of sea fog glowing pale, hiding everything beyond it; to the right, the platform's lip running a short way along the coast and ending in the sea, low ribs of black rock with still rock pools between them holding the pale sky; on the far right, the right half of the calm view directly behind the viewer: the wide wet rock floor stretching away inland, broken by low ribs of black rock and still pools, joining its other half cleanly at the seam directly behind you. The furthest point out, exposed and cold, moonlight on wet rock and white water, one caged lantern over the pit; a cold fog-desert coast in the nineteen-twenties like the Namib's diamond coast near Luderitz, at night: black wet rock, pale cream sand and many-coloured beach gravel silvered by the moon, bone-white bleached timber, rust-red iron, dark dressed stone, black glossy water, warm orange lantern light; painterly, cinematic, fine natural film grain. No people, no figures anywhere, no animals or birds, no lettering, writing, captions, numerals or text on anything, no painted signs, no flags with emblems. Night only: no daylight, no sun, no sunset or dawn glow. No palm trees, no quiver trees, no red canyon rock, no turquoise tropical water, no modern machinery, no electric lights, no power lines, no motorboats. Only ONE moon. No rock arch and no sea stack anywhere: the fog bank hides the open sea. No town and no houses on any skyline. No boat anywhere in this view. The fog bank stays well out at sea beyond the lip. No tripod over this pit. The platform's far end sinks into the sea: no shore, path or land bridge joins it to the land. Shot on a full-frame DSLR at 24mm, f/8, night at low tide under a bright full moon high in the sky over the sea to the west: cold silver-blue moonlight on wet rock and gravel, a deep blue-black sky with a scatter of stars, and warm orange pools of light from oil lanterns, high dynamic range, realistic depth of field, fine natural film grain, true-to-life colour. EDGE DISCIPLINE: the leftmost 6% and the rightmost 6% of the image must contain nothing but the plain continuous backdrop named above — no object, structure, post, path, fence, building corner, vehicle or figure may appear, begin or end inside those two margins, and no cast shadow may fall across them. Keep every object of interest well inboard. THE GROUND IS ONE SURFACE: the ground at the extreme left edge and the ground at the extreme right edge are the SAME patch of ground seen from the same standing point. Its paving, texture, colour, wetness and the base of anything resting on it must continue unbroken and perfectly aligned across that join, at the same height and the same scale on both sides. Again: the extreme left and right edges must align perfectly into the wide wet rock floor stretching away inland, broken by low ribs of black rock and still pools, calm and even, with no visible seam, join, or repetition.
